exhibits.name: Tension / integrity
exhibits.subtitle: Thirty struts. One continuous network.
exhibits.description: Separate compression members are held within a connected network of tension. Thirty struts and ninety cables make a sphere with no strut-to-strut contacts.
exhibits.credit: Fuller’s tensegrity explorations · Kenneth Snelson’s foundational contribution
exhibits.note: Independent icosahedral construction. The assembled geometry admits positive cable self-stress; this is not a loaded structural analysis. The motion is geometric: cables change length, while struts remain rigid. Sixty small collars finish the cable terminations. Three explicit display cradle arms support the assembled pose and withdraw during animation.

exhibits.name: A house that hangs
exhibits.subtitle: Dymaxion / Wichita House
exhibits.description: An open entrance, living area and kitchen lead around to a small utility room. The toilet and shower are reached through that buffer room, with no bathroom door opening into the kitchen. The bedroom has its own entrance from the shared living space.
exhibits.note: Overall diameter 36 ft and height 22 ft follow the Docomomo record. Roof curvature, window divisions and fit-out are estimated from museum photographs. Forty-eight roof gores and twenty-four floor spokes simplify the original construction. Floor spokes meet the deck underside. Furniture has complete visible supports; furnishings remain illustrative, not a historic fit-out survey. An illustrative aluminium entrance portal replaces obstructing rails and stays. The 1.18 m leaf swings inward 90 degrees, giving about 1.14 m between leaf and jamb (1.08 m at the projecting handle), with a 2.15 m clear head. Five 176 mm rises and four 290 mm goings meet a level 1.05 m landing. These are chosen working dimensions, not surveyed historic details. Glass opacity is 22%, museum glass 28%. The twelve anchor footings bear on the plinth. A user-requested illustrative domestic arrangement adds an open living/kitchen area and an independent bedroom plus a utility room leading into the toilet/shower. The former kitchen-facing bathroom doorway is closed. Partition height is 2.35 m above the floor; the bedroom and utility openings have 0.96 m clear framed widths and the bath opening 0.90 m, all with 2.10 m clear heads. A 1.04 m sliding utility leaf avoids a perimeter stay. The simplified suspension representation now runs above occupied rooms with perimeter drops; this is not a historic as-built or structurally certified arrangement.

exhibits.name: A climate of ideas
exhibits.subtitle: Montréal Biosphère
exhibits.description: Fuller and Sadao’s open geodesic frame surrounds the later environmental museum: staggered glazed galleries, an elevated belvedere, a slim circulation tower and exposed steel walkways.
exhibits.credit: Fuller & Sadao · dome; Éric Gauthier / DMA and collaborators · later museum
exhibits.note: Dome diameter 76 m and height 62 m remain nominal. The museum is a photographic architectural reconstruction from DMA and Giuliano Ottaviani’s 2017 photographs: separate slabs, beams, columns, framed glazing, terrace railings, stairs and tower. Working floor levels and plan dimensions are estimates, not measured drawings. Secondary connections, exact exhibit layouts and services are omitted. The dome remains a coarser six-frequency double-lattice study. Completion pass adds actual door openings at the stair and tower routes, a rear bridge, a continuous lift shaft, tread-bearing stair stringers and lattice footings. These remain estimated details.

exhibits.name: Living in the experiment
exhibits.subtitle: The Fuller dome home / Carbondale
exhibits.description: Bucky and Anne’s own home brought the geodesic idea down to domestic scale. Pale triangular roof panels meet five blue entrance and window bays.
exhibits.credit: R. Buckminster Fuller & Anne Hewlett Fuller · Pease prefabrication
exhibits.note: A three-frequency icosahedral cap with five clipped bays follows the visible composition. Approximate 39 ft 1 in diameter and 16 ft 6 in height follow the restoration architect’s account; bay cuts and windows are estimated. A low two-shelf library follows the preservation organisation’s library photograph; the reading desk, sliding entrance hardware and internal arrangement are illustrative. An unsubstantiated hearth placeholder has been removed. The entrance slider travels 1.02 m in full-size coordinates on two separate tracks.

exhibits.name: The Jitterbug
exhibits.subtitle: One motion. Eight rigid triangles.
exhibits.scale: Ideal geometric mechanism · edge length 2.33 m
exhibits.description: Eight triangles turn and draw inward together. The open cuboctahedron passes through an icosahedral arrangement before its twelve hinge positions pair into the six vertices of an octahedron.
exhibits.note: Exact fixed-edge coordinate construction, checked at 201 poses. Only the cuboctahedron-to-octahedron branch is shown; the subsequent tetrahedral fold is not included. Hinge positions and closing edge pairs coincide at the ideal limit; hardware thickness and clearance are not simulated. A removable clear exhibition table supports the open rest pose and is hidden during motion.

exhibits.name: One island, one ocean
exhibits.subtitle: The Dymaxion / Air-Ocean world map
exhibits.description: A faceted world opens into a connected field of continents. Twenty icosahedral faces, with the Air-Ocean split panels, unfold along a continuous tree of hinges. The coastlines travel with their rigid panels.
exhibits.credit: R. Buckminster Fuller & Shoji Sadao · Natural Earth coastline data
exhibits.note: Air-Ocean face arrangement follows the attributed d3-geo-polygon implementation. Coastlines use the Gray–Fuller equations and public-domain Natural Earth 110m land, sampled at 300 points across each face and simplified; small lakes and sub-resolution islands are omitted. Hinges are ideal; this is not a fabricated paper mechanism. A clear lectern supports the flat map and is hidden during folding.

form.method: Independent icosahedral edge rotation construction. Positive cable force densities and negative strut density solved for unloaded nominal geometry. Does not certify stability, loads or the animation path.

map.coastline: Natural Earth 110m land, 300-sample contours per face; lakes omitted

museumReconstruction.source: DMA project photographs and Giuliano Ottaviani / Divisare, 2017
museumReconstruction.accuracy: Photographic estimates; no surveyed dimensions for the museum.

entrance.interpretation: Illustrative aluminium portal and inward-swing leaf; not a measured reconstruction of historic door hardware or a structural design.

houseLayout.assumption: User-requested illustrative domestic plan; no claim of historic as-built accuracy. Simplified suspension is routed above occupied space with perimeter drops, not structurally certified.
houseLayout.access: Shared living/kitchen -> utility -> toilet/bath; bedroom remains independent.
